name: Question 2
problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/dccfcb991a6c302c522ea73381544d2e6f93b7310f54040151a00832473596b8.png)

The region enclosed by the curves $y=8x$ and $y=-{x}^{4}$ for $x\in [-2,0]$ is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the line $y=1.$ Which of the following gives the volume of the resulting solid?
worked_solution:
Let's draw our vertical arrow through the given region. The arrow should be pointing away from the axis of rotation.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/335b300d66c7a51a37d595f5fb99a281c00ec6a5be62e1be12c2a3104cd54694.png)

The vertical arrow 

- *enters* the region through the inner curve $y=-{x}^{4},$ and

- *leaves* through the outer curve $y=8x.$

Now, we can find the volume of our solid as the difference between the volumes of the solids generated by the outer and inner curves.

- **Step I.** Figure out the volume generated by the outer curve $y=8x.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/aae56ea01faa2c09f004fe2506c036f4d5e5b2e591e2e653f4794e4a3cecc309.png)

The corresponding volume is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}_{\text{outer}} & =\pi {\int }_{-2}^{0}[\,(\text{upper})-(\text{lower})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-2}^{0}[\,(1)-(8x)\,]^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-2}^{0}{[1-8x]}^{2}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step II.** Figure out the volume generated by the inner curve $y=-{x}^{4}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/635d3aabdc16fd90c2e2a06a042f98abe5dc16f1d7747394cd9083858023adee.png)

The corresponding volume is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}_{\text{inner}} & =\pi {\int }_{-2}^{0}[\,(\text{upper})-(\text{lower})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-2}^{0}[\,(1)-(-{x}^{4})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-2}^{0}{[1+{x}^{4}]}^{2}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step III.** Find the difference.

Finally, we can write the volume of the original solid as

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={V}_{\text{outer}}-{V}_{\text{inner}} \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-2}^{0}{[1-8x]}^{2}\,\text{d}x-\pi {\int }_{-2}^{0}{[1+{x}^{4}]}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-2}^{0}({[1-8x]}^{2}-{[1+{x}^{4}]}^{2})\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 2
?

The region enclosed by the curves y=8x and y=−x4 for x∈[−2,0] is rotated 2π radians about the line y=1. Which of the following gives the volume of the resulting solid?

a
π∫−20([8x−x4]2−1)dx
b
π∫−20([1−8x]2−[1+x4]2)dx
c
π∫−20(1+8x−x4)2dx
d
π∫−20(x4−8x)2dx
e
π∫−20([8x+1]2−[x4+1]2)dx
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let's draw our vertical arrow through the given region. The arrow should be pointing away from the axis of rotation.

The vertical arrow

  • enters the region through the inner curve y=−x4, and

  • leaves through the outer curve y=8x.

Now, we can find the volume of our solid as the difference between the volumes of the solids generated by the outer and inner curves.
